World.title: Iraq, Iran ink four key bilateral agreements
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq and Iran inked four agreements on Thursday focusing on transportation, rail connection, and municipal support, as well as government administration and human resource training.

The agreements were signed during meetings in Tehran between Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, with an emphasis on improving regional networks and collaborative work across borders, according to the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

Representatives from the transportation ministries of both countries signed a bilateral agreement designed to establish a structure for the international road transit of goods.

To improve rail network connectivity, the two sides signed an agreement to extend a railway connecting the Iraqi capital, Baghdad, to the Iranian city of Kermanshah. This railway will traverse the border city of Khosravi in Iran and Iraq’s Khanaqin.

Additionally, Tehran and Baghdad became sister cities after signing municipal twinning agreements and cooperative public administration training efforts.

The two countries also inked an agreement on administrative training, education, and human resource development.

The geopolitical achievement takes place as Iraq promotes an expansive economic strategy. Al-Zaidi’s visit to Tehran comes after a notable trip to the United States, where Iraq inked 48 business agreements worth over $60 billion with US corporations.

Through these diplomatic moves, Baghdad apparently aims to establish itself as a regional gateway.

World.title: Iraqi PM meets Iranian president in Tehran
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi met on Thursday with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian in Tehran, marking his first official visit to Iran since taking office.

Al-Zaidi’s reception in the Iranian capital was followed by a bilateral meeting with Pezeshkian and a joint session attended by a high-level Iraqi delegation, according to a statement issued by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

The Iraqi prime minister proposed a diplomatic initiative focused on stabilizing the region in light of recent escalations in military operations between the United States and Iran.

Al-Zaidi said in a statement on X that he will address matters of shared interest, bilateral cooperation, regional concerns, and measures to consolidate regional security and stability.

According to al-Zaidi, Iraq and Iran have a deep connection rooted in their shared history, culture, geographic closeness, and mutual interests. This relationship highlights the importance of dialogue and collaboration in achieving sustainable development for both countries and fostering stability in the region.

The discussions reportedly centered on economic agreements, especially concerning essential shared resources like gas supplies and the declining water flows in the Tigris and Euphrates rivers.

The Iraqi delegation underscored that Iraq will stay unbiased and neutral in any foreign tensions between Tehran and Washington.

This visit takes place after al-Zaidi met with US President Donald Trump in Washington, where they inked several trade and economic deals worth billions of dollars.

Following his visit to Tehran, al-Zaidi is expected to continue his regional tour, stopping in Turkey and Saudi Arabia to discuss bilateral cooperation.

World.title: Iraq’s public debt stands at 47% of its GDP
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi prime minister’s financial advisor Mazhar Saleh told Rudaw News on Wednesday that Iraq’s total public debt is approximately 47 percent of the country’s gross domestic product (GDP).

Although Baghdad can easily handle its debt burden, the country’s dependency on revenues generated from oil exports leaves its economy exposed to various external factors.

The major issues in the Iraqi economy, according to Saleh, are its reliance on oil income, the poor performance of other productive sectors, and the growing administrative costs.

To guarantee that the Iraqi economy can survive foreign shocks, the Iraqi government is working to diversify income sources, notably in the industrial, agricultural, and service sectors, as well as reforming the tax, customs, and banking systems, according to Saleh.

In late June, the Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) revealed that the country’s domestic debt rose to 95.7 trillion Iraqi dinars ($73 billion) by the end of April 2026 compared to 90.51 trillion dinars ($69.1 billion) recorded at the end of 2025, representing an increase of 5.16 trillion dinars ($3.9 billion).

In 2024, the domestic debt in Iraq stood at 83.05 trillion Iraqi dinars (approximately $63.4 billion).

According to the statistics, domestic debt increased during the first four months of 2026, while external debt dropped in comparison to prior years.

Iraq’s external debt stood at $54.101 billion in 2025, compared to $54.601 billion in 2024 and $56.207 billion in 2023, marking a total drop of $2.106 billion over two years, according to the CBI.

Senior officials in the Iraqi financial sector and representatives from Oliver Wyman, a renowned firm specializing in financial audits, emphasized the significance of developing medium-term plans customized to the nature of the debt, Iraq’s credit rating, and key global indicators.

The officials also called for drawing up budgets based on realistic evaluations of the country’s available finances and execution capabilities.

World.title: Iraqi security seizes 40 gold bars, large sums of cash in corruption case
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Supreme Judicial Council revealed on Wednesday that investigations into the case of Adnan al-Jumaili, a deputy oil minister accused of corruption, have resulted in the seizure of 13 billion Iraqi dinars (nearly $10 million), $400,000, and 40 gold bars hidden in different locations in the northern province of Salah al-Din.

The step is part of the Iraqi government’s ongoing nationwide anti-corruption campaign launched last month.

The Iraqi judiciary said in a statement that each of the gold bars weighs one kilogram. It added that security forces also seized five kilograms of gold jewelry, according to the state-run news agency (INA).

The seizures resulted from ongoing investigations into the suspect, according to the statement.

Al-Jumaili’s case is one of the most prominent corruption cases that emerged in the past few months, as the government’s campaign targets people suspected of theft and wasting public funds.

Iraqi authorities had already announced al-Jumaili’s arrest on allegations of financial and administrative corruption before the judiciary opened a broad investigation into the issue, including a review of his accounts, assets, and finances.

The Supreme Judicial Council did not provide any information on the locations where the money and gold were discovered and mentioned that search and recovery efforts are ongoing.

The Iraqi cabinet affirmed that recovering public funds is one of the priorities of its agenda, while the Federal Commission of Integrity and the judiciary are working to pursue those accused both inside and outside Iraq.

World.title: Air defenses intercept 4 drones in northern Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The international coalition’s air defense systems intercepted on Wednesday evening four drones over Erbil, the capital of the Kurdistan region of Iraq.

The systems were activated when flying objects approached the US consulate and its associated logistics base, according to Al-Arabiya News.

Four explosions were reportedly heard in the skies over Erbil following the activation of the international coalition’s air defense systems.

A security source confirmed that air defenses successfully intercepted and destroyed the drones before reaching their targets, adding that the attack caused no casualties or material damage.

On Tuesday, Iraqi security sources said that air defenses intercepted three explosive-laden drones near the US consulate in Erbil with two drones targeting a camp of the Kurdistan Freedom Party (PAK), an Iranian Kurdish opposition group.

The state-run news agency (INA) reported that Erbil International Airport temporarily suspended flights but later announced their resumption.

Iraqi air defenses shot down an explosive-laden drone on Monday near Harir Air Base in Iraq, which houses US and international coalition forces. There were no reports of casualties or damages.

No group has claimed responsibility for the attacks. Neither Iraqi officials nor the Kurdistan Regional Government (KRG) has issued a statement identifying the attackers or the types of drones involved.

The recent escalation in Iraqi Kurdistan, which largely included drone assaults over Erbil, comes amid rising tensions between the United States and Iran, the most serious since a cease-fire deal was reached in mid-June.

World.title: US dollar rises against Iraqi dinar
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate for the US dollar compared to the Iraqi dinar rose on Wednesday in the Iraqi capital, Baghdad, and the capital of the Kurdistan region of Iraq, Erbil.

The US dollar exchange rate slightly rose in Baghdad’s al-Kifah and al-Harithiya stock exchanges, reaching 1,504 Iraqi dinars compared to 1,502.5 Iraqi dinars on Wednesday’s morning.

The exchange rate in currency exchange shops in Baghdad ranged between 1,510 Iraqi dinars and 1,500 Iraqi dinars, Shafaq News reported.

In Erbil, the US dollar exchange rate also rose, fluctuating between 1,508.5 and 1,507.5 Iraqi dinars.

The Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) said in February 2023 that it has begun using the new US dollar exchange rate of 1,300 dinars to every US dollar.

The previous official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars to one US dollar, which was being exchanged in the parallel market at a rate of 1,550 dinars.

While the official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars per dollar in January 2023, the US currency was being exchanged at 1,610 dinars during the same month in the parallel market in Iraq. This variation indicated a difference of over 10 percent in the exchange rates.

World.title: PM Al Zaidi proposes joint fund in call with German Chancellor Friedrich Merz
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Prime Minister Ali Falih al-Zaidi held high-level telephone discussions with German Chancellor Friedrich Merz on Wednesday, July 22, 2026, focusing on expanding economic cooperation, trade, and industrial investment between the two nations.

According to an official statement released by the Prime Minister’s Media Office, the talks covered bilateral ties across multiple sectors, with particular emphasis on economic partnerships, trade volume expansion, direct investment, and joint migration management frameworks.

Key Discussion Pillars

Joint Iraqi-German Fund: Prime Minister Al-Zaidi proposed establishing a dedicated joint fund to finance industrial development projects in Iraq with German technical and capital backing.

Economic Reforms & Anti-Corruption: Al-Zaidi reiterated Baghdad’s commitment to eradicating administrative corruption and creating an open, transparent environment for foreign capital to diversify Iraq’s national economy.

Official Invitation to Berlin: Chancellor Merz extended a formal invitation to Prime Minister Al-Zaidi to visit Germany for an official state visit to deepen economic and political coordination.

Support for Fiscal Reform: Germany reaffirmed its support for the Iraqi government’s ongoing economic and financial reforms, expressing strong readiness from German corporations to expand investment footprints across Iraq.

The discussions highlight Baghdad’s broader diplomatic strategy of leveraging European economic integration to modernize domestic industrial infrastructure and broaden trade partnerships beyond energy exports.

World.title: Lebanon PM says Beirut working for ‘complete Israeli withdrawal’
World.content:
Zawtar al-Gharbiyah – Lebanon is working towards a “complete Israeli withdrawal” from areas it occupies, Prime Minister Nawaf Salam said on Wednesday on a visit to a village where Lebanon’s army recently deployed.

“We will continue mobilising our political and diplomatic efforts to secure a complete Israeli withdrawal from the south,” he said in Zawtar al-Gharbiya.

Israeli forces were previously present on the outskirts of the village following the war with Iran-backed Hezbollah.

Salam visited the town a day after Lebanese President Joseph Aoun met with his US counterpart Donald Trump at the White House, where he “stressed the urgent need for a full Israeli withdrawal from Lebanese territory”.

Under a US-sponsored agreement signed last month, Lebanon’s army is meant to disarm Hezbollah and the Israeli military is to withdraw from “pilot zones” where Lebanese forces will subsequently deploy.

Hezbollah has repeatedly rejected the agreement and refuses to lay down its weapons.

The military said on Tuesday that Israeli forces “opened fire” near troops deploying at Zawtar al-Gharbiya.

The Israeli military said it had only fired “warning shots into the air” after Lebanese soldiers entered an area that was “not part of the pilot area”.

Hezbollah drew Lebanon into the Middle East war by attacking Israel in support of Tehran on March 2, prompting major Israeli airstrikes and a ground invasion.

After planting a Lebanese flag in Zawtar al-Gharbiya on Wednesday, Salam said “in parallel with the army’s deployment, we will continue opening roads, removing rubble, and securing essential services, enabling our people to return safely and with dignity to their homes and villages”.

– ‘Heads held high’ –

The war caused widespread destruction, mainly in the south, though violence has declined since the signing of a framework agreement between the United States and Iran last month and the Lebanon-Israel deal.

According to the United Nations, more than 700,000 people have returned to their homes over the past few weeks.

In Zawtar al-Gharbiya, dozens of residents waited at the village’s entrance for permission to go check on their homes.

“We will enter the town with our heads held high, thanks to the presence of the Lebanese army,” Abbas Yaghi, 73, told AFP.

The military had told residents on Tuesday to avoid entering the village “until the security situation stabilises”.

The army is conducting a sweep of the town, which is geographically contiguous with its Israeli-occupied neighbour, Zawtar al-Shariqya.

Israeli troops still launch intermittent strikes in surrounding towns, the latest on Nabatieh al-Fawqa.

“We will follow the army if it gives us permission to enter,” Mostapha Ammar, a 60-year-old resident of Zawtar al-Sharqiya said, hoping that Israel would withdraw from other areas.

Wafaa Ismail, 64, also from Zawtar al-Sharqiya, was not granted permission to enter the neighbouring village as Salam visited.

She expressed frustration at seeing the prime minister enter on his own, escorted by the army, saying: “He should have brought the people in with him so he could claim victory.”

World.title: 'More strict actions to come against paper leaks': PM Modi announces new Bill push in video message
World.content:
Prime Minister assures students that strict action will be taken against paper leaks on Friday

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday announced that government will bring in more strict actions against paper leaks. In a late night video message, PM Modi said that the Union Cabinet will discuss these stringent measures on Friday and the government will try to get the Bill passed in Parliament next week.He assured that the Centre will bring in stricter measures to curb examination paper leaks, including provisions for fast-track courts and harsher punishments for offenders.His message comes amid massive nationwide protests against alleged irregularities in the NEET UG examination. "I know that paper leak is not an ordinary issue. It is very painful for lakh of students and their guardians.""Numerous effective measures have been taken in the past two and a half months since the paper leak incident. The culprits have been caught and are in jail. Our most important responsibility was to ensure that students' year is not wasted. The government used all its might to ensure that 22 lakh students could take their exams in the shortest possible time," he added.Further talking about the bill on fast track courts he added, "On the 19th July, the results were declared. I directed the departments today to establish a fast-track court. The departments presented me with the resolution late at night. This resolution, along with the provision for a fast-track court and harsh punishment, will be discussed in the cabinet tomorrow. After the suggestions of cabinet colleagues, it will be finalised, and since the second week of Parliament is starting from Monday, efforts will be made to get that bill passed in the House as soon as possible. "

World.title: CJP delegation to meet government ministers on Friday as Centre renews outreach: Report
World.content: NEW DELHI: A delegation of the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) will meet government ministers at 12.30 pm on Friday, PTI reported, citing sources, marking the first formal engagement after days of deadlock between the Centre and the student-led outfit over the alleged NEET paper leak.The meeting comes after repeated efforts by the government to initiate dialogue with the protesters. On Thursday, Union minister J P Nadda invited the CJP leadership for talks, but the offer was declined as the outfit insisted that any discussion should take place at a neutral venue near the protest site, according to PTI sources.Government sources had earlier told ANI that an offer to continue talks with the CJP leadership had also been rejected, prolonging the stalemate.CJP spokesperson Saurav Das had maintained that the group was willing to hold talks but not at a minister's residence or office. "We refused to go to anyone's house or office. The people's court is here. Ministers should come among the people. If they want to talk, it should be held at the Jantar Mantar," he had said.Das, however, said the CJP remained open to dialogue at a neutral venue if there were security concerns.The protests, centred at Jantar Mantar, have continued for nearly a month, with demonstrators demanding the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan, compensation for families of students who allegedly died by suicide over the NEET paper leak, and withdrawal of cases filed against peaceful protesters.Earlier this week, representatives of the CJP met J P Nadda and submitted their demands. According to the CJP, the Union minister assured them that the issues would be discussed at the appropriate level, ANI reported.

World.title: Centre monitoring 2,485 Himalayan glacial lakes; 56 classified as 'very high risk'
World.content:
Centre monitoring 2,485 Himalayan glacial lakes; 56 classified as 'very high risk (Image/AP)

(with inputs from PTI)

NEW DELHI: The Centre on Thursday said it is monitoring 2,485 glacial lakes spread across the Himalayan river basins using remote sensing techniques. It also informed Parliament that 56 glacial lakes have been classified as 'very high risk' following a scientific assessment conducted in 2025 due to their potential to trigger Glacial Lake Outburst Floods (GLOFs).In a written reply in the Lok Sabha, jal shakti state minister Raj Bhushan Choudhary said the Central Water Commission (CWC) monitors glacial lakes larger than 10 hectares across four states and two Union Territories from June to October every year using remote sensing.The minister said the National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA), in collaboration with national scientific agencies, carried out a scientific assessment of 189 high-risk glacial lakes across the Indian Himalayan Region in 2025."Based on the assessment, 56 glacial lakes were classified as very high risk considering their potential to trigger Glacial Lake Outburst Floods (GLOFs) and the exposure of downstream habitations and infrastructure," Choudhary said.He said the government has started establishing Glacial Lake Outburst Flood (GLOF) Early Warning Systems (EWS) at selected high-risk glacial lakes based on hazard assessments and continuous monitoring.However, the minister clarified that no end-to-end GLOF Early Warning System has been commissioned so far under the National GLOF Risk Mitigation Programme (NGRMP).Choudhary said the NDMA is implementing the NGRMP, which was approved in 2024 for Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Sikkim and Arunachal Pradesh at a cost of Rs 150 crore."The programme envisages Hazard and Risk Assessment, Monitoring and Early Warning Systems, site-specific structural and non-structural mitigation of measures, and community awareness and capacity building," he said.The minister added that Rs 52.50 crore has been allocated under the Monitoring and Early Warning System component of the programme.He also said the NDMA, along with the Swiss Agency for Development and Cooperation (SDC) and the Sikkim State Disaster Management Authority (SSDMA), carried out multi-agency expeditions to the high-risk South Lhonak and Shako Cho glacial lakes in Sikkim during 2023 and 2024. The expeditions were aimed at supporting scientific studies and developing monitoring systems, early warning mechanisms and mitigation measures.

World.title: India slams Pakistan's 'state-sponsored' misinformation at Asean, says Indus Waters Treaty in abeyance
World.content:
NEW DELHI: India on Thursday categorically rejected

's comments at the Asean Regional Forum in Manila, calling them "baseless and unwarranted".

New Delhi slammed Islamabad of using the multilateral platform to peddle "state-sponsored disinformation" and divert attention from its record of sponsoring cross-border terrorism.

"It is no surprise that a multilateral forum has once again been cynically exploited by Pakistan to amplify falsehoods, peddle state-sponsored disinformation, and divert attention from its own well-documented record of sponsoring cross-border terrorism," MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said.

"The Union Territories of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh have been, are and will always remain integral and inalienable parts of India.

Pakistan has no locus standi to comment on the same," MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said in response to media queries.

Jaiswal also said India's position on the

remained consistent, stating that the treaty stands in abeyance in response to Pakistan's continued sponsorship of cross-border terrorism, including the Pahalgam attack. "IWT will continue to be held in abeyance until Pakistan credibly and irrevocably abjures its support for cross-border terrorism," he said.





Jaiswal also condemned Pakistan's practice of propagating "officially sponsored disinformation, often dressed in religious terminology such as the use of terms like 'Fitna al-Hindustan'."

"This is a futile attempt by the Pakistani establishment to deflect attention from its own internal crises and its well-proven role as a safe haven for global terrorist networks," he said.

He added that Pakistan would serve itself better by "dismantling the infrastructure of terrorism on its soil and putting its own house in order" instead of pointing fingers at its neighbours.

External affairs minister S Jaishankar attended the foreign minister-level meetings under the Asean framework, including the Asean-India, East Asia Summit and Asean Regional Forum meetings in Manila over the last two days.

Pakistanâs deputy prime minister and foreign minister Mohammad Ishaq Dar led Pakistan's delegation at the forum. He raised the Jammu and Kashmir dispute, calling for its resolution in accordance with

resolutions, and expressed concern over India's decision to hold the Indus Waters Treaty in abeyance.

World.title: 'UP ke ladke' to take on BJP again, but who will show 'bigger heart'? Seat-sharing test awaits Rahul, Akhilesh
World.content:
NEW DELHI: What does the size of oneâs heart have to do with political alliances? Perhaps quite a lot when the allies are the

and the Samajwadi Party, and at stake is the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly election.

The âUP ke ladkeâ delivered in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. The partnership between

and

helped the INDIA bloc win 43 of Uttar Pradeshâs 80 seats, handing the

BJP

its biggest electoral setback in the state in a decade.

Now, as the two parties prepare for seat-sharing negotiations for next yearâs assembly election, leaders on both sides want the other to show a âbig heartâ and be more accommodating.

The 'UP ke ladke' proved to be a winning combination in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections.

Akhilesh made the first appeal. At the INDIA blocâs crisis meeting on June 9, held after Mamata Banerjeeâs shock defeat in West Bengal, the SP chief had a word of advice for the Congress: âShow a large heart and be accommodative.â

The message was clear: the Congress should avoid competing with regional allies and recognise their dominance in states where they remain the principal opposition force.

With the Congress facing criticism from allies over its aggressive approach during elections, Rahul responded with an emphatic assurance: âI will bear every single humiliation that I have to bear to knit this group together and make it succeed.





What is the main issue here? I have no interest in fighting you. I would have to be a madman to suddenly get up and say I am going to fight you because you are our allies, you are our friends, you are the people we love.

â

Rahulâs conciliatory message, however, has not stopped Congress leaders in Uttar Pradesh from staking an ambitious claim. They have turned the âbig heartâ argument around, asking the SP to offer the Congress equal status, a respectable deal and, according to some leaders, 50:50 parity.

Saharanpur MP Imran Masood has argued that the SP benefited more from the alliance in 2024.

Saharanpur MP Imran Masood has claimed that the SP gained more than the Congress from their alliance in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections.

Congress co-incharge for Uttar Pradesh Rajesh Tiwari made a similar argument: âThe SP is keen to head the next government in the state. Hence, it should have a big heart.â

The pitch grew louder on July 2 when newly appointed Uttar Pradesh Congress in-charge Rajendra Pal Gautam said the party would enter the assembly election on the principles of âequality and respectâ.

These remarks appear far removed from Rahulâs conciliatory intervention at the INDIA bloc meeting in June. But the posturing by Congress leaders is hardly surprising. Seat-sharing has repeatedly emerged as a point of friction between the party and its regional allies.

The same tension has surfaced in several states where the Congress has attempted to balance its national ambitions with the political dominance of regional partners.

Bihar

In Bihar, the Congress and the RJD failed to finalise a seat-sharing agreement even after nominations opened for the first phase of the assembly elections. The lack of coordination was evident when Tejashwi Yadav filed his nomination papers without any senior Congress leader by his side.

The two parties eventually reached an agreement, but the delay had already exposed divisions within the Mahagathbandhan and disrupted its preparations.

Little wonder, their Mahagathbandhan was decimated by the BJP and its allies.

Haryana

In Haryana, several rounds of negotiations between the Congress and Arvind Kejriwalâs AAP failed to produce a seat-sharing agreement. The two parties could not agree on the number and choice of constituencies, while the bitterness of their rivalry in Delhi made a compromise even more difficult.

They eventually contested separately, splitting the opposition space in several constituencies.

The Congress fell short of dislodging the BJP, which returned to power for a third consecutive term.

Madhya Pradesh

But when it comes to seat sharing with Samajwadi Party, there is already a history of bitterness between the two allies. There was an open war of words between Akhilesh Yadav and the then CM face of Congress Kamal Nath, who refused to cede any ground to the Samajwadi Party in the state. This was immediately after the opposition had joined hands at the national level under the INDIA bloc banner to fight the BJP.

Despite that the Congress high command remained a mute spectator as Kamal Nath refused to budge. Kamal Nath, who was confident of victory then, announced that the INDIA bloc was only for national elections. The bitterness complicated negotiations for the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, before an intervention by senior leaders, including Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, helped rescue the partnership.

What's happening now?

Now, as the assembly elections approach, both sides have begun posturing to keep up the pressure.

Congress leaders have been more vocal, citing the partyâs national status, as they often do when dealing with regional allies.

In fact, newly appointed Congress in-charge Rajendra Pal Gautam, who is supposed to oversee the partyâs campaign in UP, has gone on to claim that the SPâs success in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections was because the Congress was projected as the senior partner.

Gautam credited INDIA blocâs 2024 gains to Congressâs leadership, arguing that only Rahul Gandhi had national stature to take on BJP.

The Congress leader has also claimed that if the party is not given its due respect within the alliance, it would amount to giving the BJP a âwalkoverâ.

Interestingly, both parties are citing past results to justify their claims. The Congress points to the Samajwadi Partyâs performance in the 2014 and 2019 Lok Sabha elections to argue that its spectacular showing in 2024 was the result of its alliance with the grand old party.

The SP won five seats in 2014 when it contested alone and five in 2019 when it was allied with Mayawatiâs BSP. However, when the SP and Congress contested together in 2024, the SPâs tally rose to 37.

Congress leaders claim that this sharp increase was due to the influence of the grand old party.

Now, let us analyse the Congressâs performance in Uttar Pradesh assembly elections.

The Congress has been out of power in UP since 1989. Over the last four decades, its presence in the state assembly has dwindled continuously, and the party has largely been confined to the Gandhi family bastions of Rae Bareli and Amethi. In the Lok Sabha elections, the Congress won only two seats in 2014 and one in 2019, before increasing its tally to six in 2024.

The Congress and SP contested the 2017 assembly elections in alliance but were decimated by the BJP. While the SP won 47 seats, the Congress managed only seven.

In the 2022 elections, the Congress went solo. Led by AICC general secretary Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, the party contested 399 seats, with women accounting for 40% of its candidates. Despite this, the party performed poorly and its vote share fell to 2.33%.

How the SP and Congress fared when they fought separately

The Congress managed to win only two seatsâAradhana Mishra âMonaâ from Rampur Khas in Pratapgarh district and Virendra Chaudhary from Pharenda in Maharajganj district.

It marked the partyâs worst-ever assembly election performance in Uttar Pradesh.

So, will the âUP ke do ladkeâ unite again in 2027, as they did in 2024, to stun the BJP-led NDA in Uttar Pradesh? There has been considerable bonhomie on display between Rahul Gandhi and Akhilesh Yadav. The two used their birthdays, 12 days apart, to reinforce their shared commitment to fighting the BJP. But to ensure that this bonhomie translates into electoral gains for both parties, they will have to rein in their leaders, especially those in the Congress.

When the Congress surprised everyone with a sit-in protest outside Prime Minister Narendra Modiâs residence in the national capital over the NEET issue, Akhilesh was by Rahul Gandhiâs side. The two leaders have also held a closed-door meeting in Parliament, along with Priyanka Gandhi, perhaps to work out the contours of a practical seat-sharing formula acceptable to both parties.

The stakes are higher for the SP, which is in contention to form the next government in UP and knows that support from its allies could be crucial to achieving that objective.

The Congress, with just two seats in the assembly, has little to lose in the state. However, the grand old party would do well to realise that another botched alliance experiment could isolate it further within the INDIA bloc, which it leads.

The BJP in Uttar Pradesh is going through a challenging phase amid recent controversies. But chief minister

Yogi Adityanath

is leading the fight himself and has been quick to capitalise on the reported differences between the two allies.

While Congress leaders may be making strong remarks to build pressure on Akhilesh, they should realise that this ploy carries the risk of creating a perception among voters that the two allies are fighting. And if the Congress and SP lose this perception battle, winning the election could become difficult.

Bihar has already shown how damaging such an impression can be.

The SP and Congress have already shown that they can hurt the BJP when they fight together. The challenge in 2027 will be to ensure that the fight over seats does not begin before the fight for Uttar Pradesh. Whether they can set aside competing ambitions and agree on who must show the 'bigger heart' will determine if the 'UP ke ladke' can deliver again.

World.title: Watch: Gujarat rains trigger waist-deep flooding, vehicles go under
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Around 1,200 people have been rescued and hundreds more relocated as heavy rains battered south Gujarat, with Umbergaon taluka in Valsad district receiving over 1,100 mm of rainfall in just 16 hours, officials said on Thursday.

One rain-related death was reported in Tapi district. The Indian Air Force and Coast Guard have been put on alert for rescue efforts, while NDRF and SDRF teams are deployed across the affected areas.

Valsad district was the worst hit, with many talukas receiving over 600 mm of rain during the same period. A red alert for heavy to extremely heavy rainfall was in effect for Valsad, Navsari, Surat and Tapi districts.

Floodwaters submerge vehicles, roads in Vapi

Large parts of Vapi in Valsad district were inundated, with floodwaters submerging parked vehicles and disrupting normal life.

Videos from the area showed waist-deep water in residential colonies and commercial areas, with people wading through the deluge.

The Kaveri river in Navsari rose sharply, stranding 200 people across 11 villages. They were rescued and relocated to safety. In Surat, 1,500 residents were moved from low-lying areas and waterlogged localities.

Relief operations underway, CM reviews situation

Chief Minister Bhupendra Patel visited the State Emergency Operation Centre and reviewed the situation, speaking to district collectors and instructing them to move people from vulnerable areas to safer places.





He also spoke to Union Home Minister Amit Shah, who assured all necessary assistance.

Over 300 roads were temporarily closed, more than 200 state-run bus trips were affected, and power outages were reported in many areas.

Red alert continues, rescue teams on standby

The IMD has issued a red alert for Valsad, Navsari, Dangs, Surat and Tapi for Thursday and Friday. NDRF and SDRF teams are deployed across the affected districts, with additional teams on standby in Amreli, Junagadh and Bhavnagar.

Several trains to Mumbai were cancelled or short-terminated due to rising water levels along rail routes in south Gujarat.

The state has received around 36 per cent of its annual average rainfall so far, with south Gujarat recording over 62 per cent of its seasonal average.

World.title: ‘Must be handled with empathy’: BJP veteran Murli Manohar Joshi breaks ranks, backs NEET protesters
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Veteran

leader and former Union minister Murli Manohar Joshi on Thursday extended support to students protesting over the alleged NEET paper leak, saying their concerns about the examination system are "genuine" and should be addressed with empathy rather than force.

In a rare intervention from a senior BJP figure, Joshi also criticised the police action against protesting students in Delhi earlier this week, describing it as "merciless" and warning that such use of force could alienate large sections of society from the government's vision of a Viksit Bharat.

"It is painful to see young students from different parts of the country assembled for days on the streets of New Delhi.

Their anxieties and concerns regarding the examination system are genuine and must be handled with empathy and a desire to find a lasting solution," Joshi said in a post on X.

"It is very painful to see that even young girls were brutally mishandled," he added.

Calling for a more humane approach, Joshi said, "I fervently hope that this is not treated merely as a law-and-order issue to be tackled through the use of force."





He further warned that such action "shall alienate large sections of Indian society from the national goal of Viksit Bharat."

BJP, opposition continue war of words

Joshi's remarks came amid an intensifying political confrontation over the alleged NEET paper leak and the ongoing Monsoon Session of Parliament.

The BJP accused the

of avoiding a discussion on the issue in Parliament despite the government expressing readiness for a debate. BJP president Nitin Nabin said the opposition was "running away" from a discussion because its "double standards" would be exposed.

"The NDA government is fully prepared to hold discussions at every level on the future of students and youngsters," Nabin said, while challenging the opposition to participate in a debate on NEET and other issues concerning students.

Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman also asserted that the Centre had already taken action against those accused in the alleged paper leak and remained committed to ensuring justice for students.

She accused the Congress of pursuing "disruptive politics" instead of participating in a parliamentary discussion.

Commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal appealed to the opposition not to politicise the issue, saying the government would take the "strictest possible action" against those found guilty in paper leak cases.

Earlier in the day, Prime Minister Modi issued his first public response to the ongoing agitation, announcing that the government would set up fast-track courts to ensure swift punishment for those involved in paper leak cases.

"Nothing is more important than the welfare and future of our youth! We have decided to set up fast-track courts to ensure swift and stringent punishment for those involved in paper leaks. Have directed the concerned authorities and officials to take all necessary steps. Those who try to harm the future of our youth will not be spared," PM Modi wrote on X.

Opposition backs students, Parliament remains deadlocked

Meanwhile, opposition parties have continued to press for the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan and have linked the issue to the alleged assault on student protesters.

Leader of opposition

said INDIA bloc leaders were heading to Gandhi Smriti to express solidarity with students affected by the alleged paper leak and those injured during police action.

"India's students are not alone. The entire Opposition stands with them and their demands," Gandhi wrote on X.

The Opposition has made Pradhan's resignation and a discussion under Rule 267 in the Rajya Sabha key demands before agreeing to a debate, while the government has maintained that it is willing to discuss the issue without preconditions.

The deadlock has repeatedly disrupted proceedings in both Houses of Parliament.

World.title: Tanul Thakur On The Corporate Cruelty Driving The H-1B Visa Economy
World.content:
Tanul Thakurâs 'Wild Wild East' Uncovers the Human Cost of the American Dream

Excerpts:

Q:

How did this book come about?

A

:

I was an H1B worker in the US from 2011 to 2013. And during my time there as an electrical engineer, I got more than a whiff that there was some scam going on in the H1B visa programme...

And this idea really stayed with me, this idea of primarily Indians exploiting Indians in the US.

Cut to a few years later, I returned to India to pursue my passion of being a full-time writer and a journalist. And this idea then really thundered back to me in all its different manifestations... I think subconsciously I wanted to write a book that would explore morality, enslavement, identity of modern day Indian elites...

The actual story though snowballed into a much bigger and much more significant something...

This started off as a very literary project... I wanted to write a "non-fiction novel"... Then these questions started to ping my conscience: why do we not know about this scam? Who benefits from it, apart from the obvious corporate American entities? And then I figured out that this is not just about a few individuals or a few firms.





It's essentially like an entire society colluding to both perpetrate and also hide the scam.

.. You have these immigration forums, anonymous people with fake monikers talking about how they scam the system. You have visa mills and a bunch of parties coming together to perpetrate something really, really horrific. So the book changed during the process. I changed during the process.

Q: I

t

was

as if your mind

was

exploding

and you had to put it out there to say,

what on earth

are we living side by side with?

A

:

Sometimes it felt like a science fiction story... I was constantly taken aback, not just by the brazenness of the scam, but also about how this was hiding in plain sight... On the one hand, you are seeing all these crazy things that are happening, and on the other, there's absolute silence about it in the outer world... There were many heartbreaking things that I found... I was very surprised by the kinds of entities that I used to consider heroes.

Say the American media, academia, some politicians â most of them turned out to be villains... Just understanding how it is humanly possible for human beings, in this case three protagonists, to absorb so much of pain, to absorb so much of anguish... on a day to day basis and yet have the courage to solder on. These are the things that really stayed with me.

Q: W

hat exactly is the

business

model of a desi

consultancy

?

A

:

Think of it as a chain of blocks. So essentially you have a client, which is to say like a Fortune 500 firm or a corporate America entity which wants â I mean back in 2010 or something â let's say wanted a Java specialist.

So it would ask a big outsourcing giant, which is called a prime vendor, do you have a Java specialist for this kind of a contractual position? If they do, they supply that. If they don't, that's when the desi consultancy model comes in, it would ask a smaller outsourcing or a staffing company.

And that's how the chain gets built. You have a client, you have a prime vendor, then you have one or two companies in between. Then you have an H1B employer who is sponsoring the visa for an H1B worker.

Now, a decade ago, if a client was paying around $120 per hour for a Java specialist or for an IT specialist with six years of experience, different parties would take a cut and the H1B worker would get somewhere around $25 an hour.

And amidst that, there is insane amounts of wage theft. You have your purchase orders being edited, you have no idea how much your employer is getting... There is this thing called benching, wherein you're supposed to pay the H1B worker when he or she doesn't have a project.

But that never happens. In fact, you don't just not get paid when you're benched. You have to pay your employers taxes during that period. There is this immense amount of psychological cruelty that's meted by Indian owners of body shops or desi consultancies to Indian H1B workers.

This dehumanization exists at varying levels. There's this literal and metaphorical transformation of identity. You are often handed a resume which has seven or eight years of fake experience.

Then you get a job through a proxy interview. Even at the client side, if you don't know anything, you have this process of like on job support where you can outsource your job to some other techie in India. So very rampant exploitation almost becomes the language of this industry.

Q: How did you persuade the protagonists to talk to you?

First of all, they were themselves so frustrated... Nobody thought their stories were stories.

Nobody thought of them as people. So the very fact that I told them that I'm interested in this, that I completely understand your pain, anguish, maybe it had kind of helped that I had done some bit of my own research... I think it was just my persistence. And I think in that persistence, they had seen some bit of my wonder, my innocence, my intellectual curiosity, but also my rage, my very incipient rage.

.. They all got eased into the process because I think they had understood that he's not a regular journalist, which is to say that he genuinely cares for us as people...

I think being genuinely open, innocent and curious about their lives as people and applying largely the same matrices, but icing it with a copious amount of rage about the systemic abuse itself, I think kind of endeared them to talk to me.

Q: T

his H1B

scam

is

kind of a

parallel economy which

seems to have

no closure to it.

A

:

What occurred to me around 2020 is that this is a book about the tyranny of capitalism. It's about the tyranny or the dictates of American neoliberalism.

And I am essentially just using H1B as a metaphor or as a lens to explore that... One can very easily and glibly dismiss a lot of American workers as racist or bigoted or xenophobic. Some of them could be, sure. But many of them are actually not just these things. They are simply very saddened about their economic and psychological and personal devastation.

But that's also one of the biggest corporate cruelties, right? Or it's one of the biggest corporate tricks... A lot of Americans are just blaming Indians, which is insane to me because given the way this H1B system has been abused... they should not be each other's adversaries. They should understand that they are both being pitted against each other... This is something that I want a lot of people to understand, that this is essentially not about immigrants versus citizens, it's about immigrants and citizens versus exploitative corporations and the exploitative American capitalist structure itself.

World.title: Protesters, petrol pump, police... and one woman
World.content:
The national capital has seen heavy clashes between Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) protesters and Delhi Police personnel even as activist Sonam Wangchuk continued his hunger strike to demand educational reform.

CJP protest in Delhi: Pictures show you what happened on July 20, 2026

The area around Janpath station of the Delhi Metro saw widespread protests, on July 20, 2026, along with repeated lathi-charge by the Delhi Police.

While on the site on July 20, 2026, The Hindu came across a petrol pump. A Bharat Petroleum fuel station. The signs of violence were visible.

On July 21, 2026, The Hindu visited the spot again. The shattered glass still existed. The pump is also a vehicle detailing studio owned by Siddharth and Sarvgun Puri (names changed). The incident happened two days before the inauguration of their store.

Jantar Mantar LIVE updates

Upon being asked for proof, Mr. Siddharth, 30, pulled up CCTV videos on his phone.

CJP’s ‘night vigil’ at Jantar Mantar: In pictures

He said that the violence “started at 6:28 p.m.” and till then they were “providing first aid” to all, along with “washroom services”. Siddharth says “till 5.30-6 p.m.” it was all “peaceful”.

Within four hours, the scene had changed.

The Hindu asked the owners if they had reached out to the police. Mr. Siddharth said that they had gone to file an FIR, and was provided with the number of the investigating officer (IO). He added that he will now file an “online FIR”.

One person against the violence

After talking to the employees of the petrol pump who were present at the site during the incident, The Hindu found out that when the chaos began, all of them sought safety and shelter.

Except one woman.

S., 40, was the only one who did not run. This has been corroborated by her colleagues.

“Bache protest kar rhe the. Police ne unpar lathi charge kar diya. Bache idhar udhar bhaage, (Kids were protesting, the police lathi-charged on them. Kids ran here and there),” she said.

“Kuch bache thak chuke the toh woh baith gaye. (Some kids were tired, and they sat down),” she said pointing to a spot on the ground inside the petrol pump.

“Police jab andar aayi hai lathi charge karti hui aur unhone yahan bhi bachon ko maarna shuru kara toh woh udhar bhaag gaye. Aur jab udhar se saare bache aaye bhaage hue, jahan se bhi laaye the pathar toh police vaale idhar bhaage hain”(pointing towards inside the pump premises (When the police came inside doing lathi charge, they also started beating up the kids. So (kids) ran. When the kids brought back stones from wherever they had procured, that is when the police personnel ran here).”

“Woh pathar unke maar rhe the woh, lekin woh phir achanak yahan bhi lag gye. (They were throwing stones at them but it also hit here),” said S. while recounting how the window pane got broken by stones thrown by the protesters.

They were meant for the police personnel and inadvertently hit the window panes of the pump, she added.

“Mein toh wahin khadi ho kar rokti rahi. Baaki toh sab chup hi gaye the, lekin merse nahin jaaya gaya ki bachein hain kahin gir pad ke lag na jaaye. Vaise hi itni chote khaa chuke hain woh. (I kept standing there and stopping them. Everyone else had already hidden, but I could not leave because they are kids; they might get hurt after falling. They had already suffered such wounds).”

“Ab mein medicines rakhti hoon apne saath (I keep medicines with myself),” S. said, a day after the incident. She showed The Hindu the medicines that she carries in her pocket and the ones she said she used to “treat the kids”.

Upon being asked the reason for her courage against bipartisan violence. S. replied with just one sentence.

“Kyunki mein maa hoon. Mere bhi do bache hain. (I also have two kids. Because I am a mother).”

World.title: PM Modi promises 'more strict actions against paper leaks' amid CJP protests
World.content:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday (July 23, 2026) promised that “more strict” action would be taken against paper leaks as the CJP-led protests continue over the alleged irregularities in the NEET-UG 2026 examination.

In a self-recorded video shared on X, the Prime Minister announced that the Union Cabinet will take up a draft Bill providing for Fast-Track Courts and stringent punishment for offenders. he said, “I have issued directions to departments to set up Fast-Track Courts”

The Opposition has been demanding the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan and a detailed discussion on the NEET paper leak issue in the ongoing Monsoon Session of Parliament, with the controversy triggering protests inside and outside the House.

Along with the video, the Prime Minister wrote, “More strict actions against paper leaks to come in tomorrow’s Cabinet!”

In the video, Mr. Modi said, “Friends, I know that paper leaks are not an ordinary matter. For lakhs of students and their parents, it is extremely painful. And that is why, in the last two and a half months since the paper leak incidents, several major steps have been taken. The culprits have been caught; they are currently in jail,” he said.

PM said, “Our most important responsibility was to ensure that a whole year for the students is not wasted. It was very important to conduct the exams immediately. The government used its full strength to arrange exams for nearly 22 lakh students in the shortest possible time. And just five or six days ago, on the 19th, the results were also announced. News of the happiness of successful students is coming from all over the country.”

Stressing that the government was not stopping there, PM Modi said, “However, we are not among those who are satisfied with just that. And therefore, today I have issued directions to the departments to set up Fast-Track Courts. The departments worked tirelessly and, late last night, provided me with a draft. This draft, which includes provisions for Fast-Track Courts and stringent punishments, will be discussed in the Cabinet tomorrow,” he said.

The PM further said, “After incorporating suggestions from Cabinet colleagues, it will be given a final shape. Efforts will be made to get this Bill passed in the House as soon as possible, as the second week of the Parliament session begins on Monday.”

Mr. Modi said, “Nothing is more important than the welfare and future of our youth! Those who try to harm the future of our youth will not be spared.”

Earlier in the day, Prime Minister Narendra Modi broke his silence on the controversy, announcing that the government would establish fast-track courts to ensure swift punishment for those involved in examination paper leaks.

World.title: All roads continue to lead to Jantar Mantar
World.content:
The gap between the police barricades and the swelling line of protesters became all too stark on Thursday with both sides zealously guarding their end of Sansad Marg. While thousands of protesters continued to occupy a stretch of the Sansad Marg – leading from Connaught Place to Tolstoy Marg – security forces and riot control vehicles stood guard at the rest of the arterial road leading to Parliament House.

Following minor clashes between the police and Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) protesters the previous night, security was stepped up on Thursday and Internet was suspended around the area. CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke told the media that “Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) goons” have infiltrated the protest and are engaging in stone-pelting. “People are being sent from outside to deliberately disrupt the protest. We have been sitting here for a month. No such incident has happened in a month. But now, as this protest has grown, goons are being sent from outside by the BJP to deliberately incite people and are pelting stones. The police bring trucks of stones here and then the BJP’s goons pelt these stones to defame the people of CJP.”

As thousands continued to gather at Jantar Mantar, CJP volunteers formed a human chain separating the protesters and the police. “They have been here since last night and throughout the day too. There has been no untoward incident so far today,” a police officer on duty said.

Regular cellular service was patchy at the protest site. The Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) has issued orders since July 22 to suspend Internet services in and around a 1.5 km radius of Jantar Mantar. The latest order under The Telecommunications (Temporary Suspension of Services) Rules, 2024, was effective till 12 a.m., Thursday. The previous order, issued on July 22, blocked Internet in the area for 12 hours till 6 a.m. on Thursday. It was further suspended from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. on Thursday and extended till 12 a.m. by invoking another order under the 2024 provision.

The groundswell

The crowd kept swelling through the day despite the authorities shutting down 16 metro stations and the police stopping students travelling in autorickshaws from reaching the protest site citing prohibitory orders.

Around 2.30 p.m. near Nizamuddin, the Delhi police set up two barricades and were stopping autorickshaws with young people going to the protest site about 5 km away.

“We are only stopping students who are going for the protest as ‘Section 144’ [now Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita] is in place. We are making them understand that they could get injured over there,” a police officer at Nizamuddin said, adding that they were not stopping other vehicles or people in autorickshaws going for other work.

A group of students who were removed from their autorickshaw said the police were not letting them walk towards Jantar Mantar either.

At Jantar Mantar, several people said they faced difficulties as the metro stations were shut. Simran Kaur, 21, a Delhi University student, and her friend got down at the New Delhi metro station and walked for about 3 km to reach the protest site. “Autos were not coming to this area and we had no other option,” she said.

Vishwamohini, 19, a BA History (Hons) student, said she took a bike taxi to reach the protest. “There were a lot of diversions and it took longer than usual and we had to walk the last bit.”

“Despite 16 metro stations being closed and students being stopped on their way to the protest site for the second consecutive day, thousands are still here. The actual size of the protest is much, much bigger as a lot of people are not able to reach here. The crowd you see here is only the tip of the iceberg,” said N. Sai Balaji, former All India Students’ Association national president, who has been at the protest site since the stir began on June 20.

World.title: Students see ‘familiar playbook’ as DU, colleges endorse govt. action
World.content:
With a nationwide protest call on Friday, Delhi University on Thursday evening asked its students to “stay away from Jantar Mantar” and prioritise safety and compliance with the law. The advisory comes amid criticism from students and teachers after the university and some colleges backed the government’s actions.

In a post on X, the university said unlawful assemblies at Jantar Mantar, which are strictly regulated as per Supreme Court directives, may invite legal action, and urged students to avoid the area. “Such activities can also pose serious risks to students’ personal safety and significantly impact their academic progress and professional opportunities,” it added.

Earlier, the university had said “vested interests” were exploiting students’ fears, while some college principals expressed support for Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan. Students and faculty members said these responses reflect a “familiar playbook”.

In a post on Wednesday, Delhi University said it recognised students’ pain and anxiety but added that “vested interests” were exploiting their fears instead of easing them.Soon after, Shyam Lal College and Shaheed Bhagat Singh College posted messages backing Mr. Pradhan, praising his role in driving education reforms under the NEP.

On Thursday, the university welcomed the government’s decision to set up fast-track courts for paper leak cases and urged activist Sonam Wangchuk to end his fast in the interest of students.

Parichay, a second-year law student, said principals were “not realising that students’ frustrations have gone beyond campus” and added that the administration had “lost credibility”. Another student, Kanikshka Jinwal, said she did not see a future for herself in the country and that authorities appeared indifferent to students, including those injured during the violence.

With the new academic session set to begin on July 28, discussions around the protests have intensified within colleges. “They have no academic grounds to justify such posts on official handles meant for admission and administrative information,” said Rajesh Jha, a professor at Rajdhani College. Arun Kumar Attree, Principal of Shaheed Bhagat Singh College, said the administration backed the government after interacting with students, citing unrest on campus and lack of awareness about the steps being taken.

World.title: Shops, eating joints in CP close early, count losses
World.content:
In an unprecedented move, shops, offices and restaurants in Connaught Place (CP) shut by 6.30 p.m. on Thursday following an advisory issued by the New Delhi Traders Association (NDTA), citing the prevailing situation in and around the area.

Hundreds of people have been gathering near Jantar Mantar since July 20 over the NEET paper leak and demands for the resignation of the Union Education Minister, with crowds spilling beyond the designated protest site.

In a circular issued on Thursday, the NDTA said the decision was taken after telephonic advice from the Chairperson and Vice-Chairperson of the New Delhi Municipal Council (NDMC), who asked that all commercial establishments in CP close by 6.30 p.m.

NDTA president Atul Bhargava said the advisory was issued “keeping in mind the tense situation around Jantar Mantar and CP”. The association urged all shop owners, offices and restaurants to cooperate and strictly comply with the directions.

The circular cited a “critical situation” in the area due to the Cockroach Janta Party-led (CJP) protest, and asked establishment owners to ensure compliance to avoid any untoward incident, including loss of property or injury.

While the advisory was issued for Thursday, Mr. Bhargava told The Hindu that a similar direction could be considered on Friday after reviewing the situation. He said there are around 1,400 shops and over 1,000 offices in the area.

“The traders have been reporting losses of around 20–35% over the past three days. The number of protesters near CP is also increasing, so it is in everybody’s best interest to close shops despite the losses. No damage has been reported so far. We will assess the situation tomorrow and decide,” he said.

Responding to the advisory, the Cockroach Janata Party, in a post on X, questioned the move: “Order to close all shops in Connaught Place by 6:30 p.m. this evening, what does the government want to do?”

Former Delhi Chief Minister and Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) national convenor Arvind Kejriwal also raised concerns over the security arrangements. “Order to close all shops in CP by 6:30 p.m. this evening and intense security. Piles of ambulances. Will the Central government once again act against students at Jantar Mantar today?” he said in a post on X.

World.title: Volunteers scan crowd for unwanted elements, police in plainclothes
World.content:
Three days after Delhi Police mounted baton charges and fired tear gas on protesters during the Cockroach Janta Party’s ‘Sansad Chalo’ march, volunteers at Jantar Mantar are not taking any chances. On Thursday, almost a km-long human chain shielded and guided the protesters up to the entry and exit points, with volunteers carefully scanning the crowd for unwanted elements. They also ensured that security personnel in plainclothes and without name badges do not enter the protest site disguised as commoners.

“We have formed human chains to keep the protest peaceful and maintain discipline. We are also making sure women, children, and older people stay safe and no one is passing any derogatory remarks,” said Hari Iqbal, a volunteer from Bihar who joined the demonstration from the first day on June 20.

As the day progressed, the crowd at the protest site swelled with a steady stream of students walking in for the first time. “I was a little apprehensive of the policemen,” said Anu, a Delhi University student. “A friend of mine got thrashed by police on Monday and many of them were not wearing name tags, badges and some were even in plainclothes. I was afraid I might face the same but the volunteers are actually protecting women and girls and encouraging them to move forward, away from the crowd,” she added.

But once inside, the atmosphere was not so tense as volunteers from an Anand Vihar gurdwara distributed langar in one corner. A little distance away, a non-profit medical charity provided free aid to those in need.

In another corner, volunteers were seen clearing the garbage on the site. “This is the beauty and success of this protest,” said Geegraj, a volunteer from Rajasthan who came to support the student movement following the death of a NEET aspirant in the State.

“The movement has sustained due to the discipline of those who have been part of it. Anyone who supports the protest also acknowledges the peaceful nature of it. It has to be non-violent. There is anger and rage among the crowd for sure but it needs proper guidance and that is what we are here for,” he said.

World.title: Jantar Mantar protest LIVE: Wangchuk breaks 26-day fast; relieved, says CJP founder Dipke, but vows to continue protest till Pradhan resigns
World.content:
Activist Sonam Wangchuk has broken his fast, announced Leh Apex Body co-convenor Cherring Dorjay Lakruk late on Thursday (July 23, 2026). Mr Wangchuk broke the fast in the presence of two Union Ministers on certain conditions, he said. The government gave a written assurance that cases against students will be taken back if they are not violent, he added. Also, the government gave a written assurance that they will consider compensation for NEET aspirants who took their lives, he said.

Also late on July 23, 2026, Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday (July 23, 2026), through his social media posts, sought to address student concerns on NEET paper leaks. He said, “I am deeply aware that a paper leak is no ordinary lapse; it is an injustice that inflicts severe distress upon millions of aspiring students and their families. It is in response to this gravity that we have executed swift, uncompromising measures over the past two and a half months. The offenders have been arrested, and they now stand behind bars.

Also read: The cockroach dilemma facing India’s political parties

Earlier in the day, Mr. Modi announced fast-track courts to ensure swift punishment for paper leaks. The Delhi High Court, in another late night development, designated Judge Anu Grover Baliga as Special Judge of the fast-track court to deal with criminal cases arising out of paper leaks and the use of unfair means in public examinations.

Also Read: 16 metro stations, including Rajiv Chowk, Patel Chowk, Delhi Gate and Central Secretariat, closed, says DMRC

Meanwhile, a government source said a delegation of the Cockroach Janta Party will meet with Ministers on Friday (July 24, 2026), sources said. The meeting would take place at 12.30 p.m., but its venue has not been disclosed. The CJP is yet to comment on this.

World.title: Hundreds gather in Kerala’s Kochi to express solidarity with Delhi student protest
World.content:
Hundreds, including techies, students, writers, artistes, and activists gathered here on Thursday (July 23, 2026) in solidarity with the ongoing student protests in New Delhi, triggered by the NEET question paper leak.

At the Kerala High Court Junction, the supporters held copies of the Indian Constitution and raised slogans extending the demands raised by the students protesting in New Delhi. Actor Mathew Thomas urged everyone to higlight the issues raised by the student protesters and to provide maximum coverage for them through various platforms.

Writer N.E. Sudheer said the country should be not be left to fascist ideals propagated by the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh and the Bharatiya Janata Party. He said the Indian Constitution guarantees the rights to hold peaceful protests against injustice.

Techies from Infopark came together in support of the student protest in New Delhi. They held placards against police brutality on student protesters. Anish Panthalani, president of Progressive Techies collective, said that students were protesting in New Delhi against flaws in the country’s education system, marked by paper leaks and corruption. He condemned police action against the protesters while stating that it was in violation of the basic rights of citizens.

Techies, who participated in the protest near the open gym at Infopark, said the students protesting in the national capital must get justice. They are fighting for justice, and everyone should support them, they added.

The Students’ Federation of India (SFI) and the Kerala Students’ Union (KSU) also staged demonstrations expressing solidarity with the student protest.

The march taken out by activists of the SFI to the BSNL office in the city demanding the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan was stopped by the police. Tension flared up after the agitators tried to pull down barricades. The police fired tear-gas shells to disperse the activists. Some protesters were taken into custody. Though the activists dispersed after tear gas shells were fired, they rallied again and shouted slogans at the police and against the Union government.

KSU activists staged protests across campuses in Ernakulam as part of the State-wide education bandh against alleged attempts by the Centre to clamp down on student protest demanding the resignation of Mr. Pradhan.

World.title: Sonam Wangchuk ends 26-day fast, cites ‘long negotiation’ on conditions, ‘possible violence’ in country
